draft:
Greenwich House Theater on Barrow Street is a small room, and Joseph Medeiros uses every inch of it. The stage when I got there was covered in props, costumes, signs, rugs, instruments, and what looked like the contents of several storage units arranged with careful intention. A drum kit upstage. Guitars on stands. A suitcase labeled ODYSSEUS. Signs for characters. Watermelon. The setup alone told me this wasn't going to be a fixed-position show, and I wasn't going to be able to predict where the frame would come from.

The piece is Medeiros performing Book 2 of Homer's Odyssey in Ancient Greek, solo, for an audience sitting close enough to touch him. It's part of a larger project, a lifelong one by his own account, to perform the entirety of the poem as a 24-hour solo work in the original language. Matchbook Fest, presented by Mix and Match Productions, bills itself as a space to discover new work in development, and this qualified: ambitious in the way that projects nobody's quite done before tend to be.

What I noticed in the first few minutes was where the energy would concentrate. With one performer and a room that size, the question isn't whether there's something to capture, it's whether I could stay loose enough to follow where it went. Medeiros didn't stay in one register for long. He'd be playing Odysseus with a prop staff, in full earnest, and then slide into a suitor, and then into something between a game show host and a Greek chorus, and the gear change was fast.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-78.jpg | A male performer in a dark t-shirt reading "ODYSSEUS" grips a long wooden staff horizontally across his body with both hands, face turned away, on a small stage with an amp and suitcase labeled "ODYSSEUS" visible behind him]

The ODYSSEUS suitcase showed up in a few frames as a kind of running visual anchor, the label on it doing double duty as character marker and comedy prop. I was working around the edge of the seated audience, moving when Medeiros moved, trying to stay ahead of the moment rather than chase it. When he had the staff and was working the big gestures, there was room to pull back and get the full body in a wider shot. When he came down to the floor and got close to the front rows, I had to work tight or I'd lose him in the audience.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-92.jpg | A male performer in a black t-shirt crouches over a wooden chest on stage, grinning toward the audience, a Sonor drum kit visible behind him]

The costume changes were fast and announced character. He put on a headband reading ATHENA in rhinestone letters with a pink jersey that said TELEMACHUS and turned the stage into something between a stadium and a temple. Arms wide, one finger up, a grin. The audience was close enough that I couldn't always get a full shot without someone's head coming in from the foreground, which meant working with the sightlines the room gave me rather than the ones I'd have preferred.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-167.jpg | A male performer wearing a sparkly "ATHENA" headband and a red jersey throws one arm up and extends the other to the side, smiling wide, on a stage cluttered with props, instruments, and framed photos on the back wall]

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-175.jpg | Wide shot of a small theater, performer in a tank top and red sash mid-stride on a brightly lit stage, audience silhouettes in the foreground, ceiling fan and colorful stage dressing visible]

There's a section that involved a watermelon being destroyed. I don't mean that metaphorically. By the time he was on his knees squeezing watermelon over himself and the stage, wearing a shirt that said ANOTHER ONE OF THE SUITORS, the show had moved pretty far from what most people associate with Homer. I held on the moment and let it run. The mess was real, the concentration was real, and the image reads as both at once.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-148.jpg | A male performer kneeling on stage, shirt soaked and marked, squeezes a piece of watermelon over chunks of the fruit on the floor in front of him, face downward, in intense concentration]

What I was dealing with was a show where the performer kept earning moments I hadn't set up for. He'd go quiet and close to the ground and I'd be holding for something specific, and then he'd be standing on a platform with one arm raised and I'd have thirty seconds to reposition. That's a different condition than a concert or even most theater, where blocking tends to repeat. Nothing here repeated quite the same way twice.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-111.jpg | A male performer in a grey t-shirt and blue shorts stands on a raised platform with one arm raised, holding a microphone, turned slightly to the side, audience silhouettes in the foreground, photos and lamps on the dark back wall]

For organizations like Mix and Match Productions bringing work in development to a venue like Greenwich House, stills are what documentation of the developmental moment looks like. Grant committees and presenting partners don't get to see the show; they see whatever was captured. Having photos from a performance that was already this fully realized gives the production something to work with as it moves forward.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-113.jpg | A male performer in a white tank top holds a black case labeled "ODYSSEUS" in both hands, crouching slightly, looking offstage with focused expression, backstage dressing and coatrack visible behind him]

If you're producing new work or solo performance and want photography that keeps up when the show doesn't stay still, get in touch.
corrected:
The One-Man Odyssey at Greenwich House Theater

The One-Man Odyssey was part two of Matchbook Spark Vol. 2, presented by Mix and Match Productions at The Greenwich House Theater, paired with BLUDLINE: A Hip-Hop Odyssey. Joseph Medeiros performs Book 2 of Homer's Odyssey in Ancient Greek, solo. Matchbook Fest bills itself as a place to see new work in development.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-175.jpg | Wide view of Greenwich House Theater, Joseph Medeiros mid-stride in a tank top and red sash, audience silhouetted in the foreground]

I worked mostly from the back of the house, with room to move along the back wall and down house right. Going down that side put the edge of the stage in frame, the dressing area and a coatrack behind him.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-113.jpg | Joseph Medeiros in a white tank top holds a black ODYSSEUS case, looking offstage, backstage dressing visible at Greenwich House Theater]

Medeiros plays every character himself. Aegyptius with a staff, then straight out to the audience a beat later, and the switches came fast.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-78.jpg | Joseph Medeiros grips a wooden staff across his body, face turned away, on the small stage at Greenwich House Theater]

Props and costume did most of that work. A staff, a chest, a rhinestone headband reading ATHENA, a red jersey reading TELEMACHUS.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-92.jpg | Joseph Medeiros crouches over a wooden chest, grinning toward the audience, drum kit behind him, at Greenwich House Theater]

From the back of the house, anything wide picked up heads in the foreground, so I worked with the sightlines the room gave me instead of the ones I'd have picked. At one point he came off the stage and into the audience.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-167.jpg | Joseph Medeiros in a rhinestone ATHENA headband and red TELEMACHUS jersey, arms raised, on the prop-filled stage at Greenwich House Theater]

The watermelon came out partway through. By the time he was on his knees squeezing it over himself and the stage in a shirt that read ANOTHER ONE OF THE SUITORS, the show was a long way from what most people picture when they hear Homer.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-148.jpg | Joseph Medeiros kneeling in a soaked shirt, squeezing watermelon over the stage floor at Greenwich House Theater]

The one raised platform put him above the audience. It was the only point in the night with nothing between him and the lens.

[PHOTO: The One-Man Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-111.jpg | Joseph Medeiros stands on a raised platform with a microphone, one arm up, audience silhouetted in the foreground at Greenwich House Theater]

For work still in development, the photos are what everyone who wasn't in the room ends up seeing. Grant panels and presenting partners don't get to attend. They see whatever was captured, and that becomes the record of where the piece was at this stage.

If you're developing new work and need it documented, get in touch.
